guidance.statement: 2.5 bps payment processing margin upside from MDR on UPI implementation.
guidance.quote: We've clearly come out of this question of whether Paytm can make profit or not... 2.5 bps is something that we can make.
guidance.speaker: Vijay Shekhar Sharma

growth_commentary: Business model is compounding from previous years with strong performance in credit distribution and payment processing.
Reported two consecutive quarters of 28% year-on-year revenue growth, with like-for-like numbers (excluding PIDF) in the 30s.
Merchant and personal loan distribution businesses continue to perform very well with strong structural tailwinds.
AI integration across sales, collections, and operations has improved efficiency and accelerated revenue realization.

pushback.question: How will the 2.5 bps payment processing margin from UPI MDR flow through to EBITDA, and will it be offset by consumer acquisition investments?
pushback.answer: Management stated that the 2.5 bps is bottom-line accretive and independent of consumer acquisition strategies, which remain focused on market share growth.

pushback.question: Why was P2M GMV flat sequentially this quarter, and is it a sign of weakness?
pushback.answer: Management explained they deliberately chose to walk away from large enterprise and online merchants with negative contribution margins to prioritize profitable GMV and unit economics.

pushback.question: Why do lending partners flip-flop on Default Loss Guarantee (DLG) requirements, and how does it impact profitability?
pushback.answer: Management noted that DLG changes have a direct upfront impact on contribution margin and EBITDA in the specific quarter due to conservative accounting, but overall business momentum easily absorbs the drag.
